document_title: Fairbanks Votes Tuesday. Six Voices on AI Data Centers
post_copy:
The only item on both halves of Fairbanks' priority list is a data center moratorium. The land offered for AI is the Air Force's.

The October 6th vote doesn't decide whether data centers come. It picks who asks the borough's questions.

The moratorium is a request among 25 priorities. Its text names state-owned or municipal lands. The Air Force offered to lease about 4,700 acres for AI data centers, including Eielson inside the borough.

Miguel Ramirez and Alexis Howell, Nick LaJiness and Shelly Shupe, Scott Crass and Joshua Leaders run for three Assembly seats. None of the six told Alaska's News Source they support data centers.

Four frames give all six candidates equal room. One maps Eielson inside the borough.

Which of electrical demand, water, noise and air quality should the winners take to the Air Force first?

#FNSBAssembly #FairbanksVotes #EielsonAFB

aftercare: Post Monday, October 5th, or early on Tuesday, October 6th, ideally 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time and in any case before polls close at 8 p.m. that Tuesday. October 6th is election day, so this deck only works before the vote. Once polls close, 'Tuesday' in the document title and on slides 01, 08 and 09 is wrong, and the deck shouldn't be posted as is. Posting cadence is your call.

On LinkedIn, start a post, choose Add a document, upload the deck PDF and set the document title to Fairbanks Votes Tuesday. Six Voices on AI Data Centers. Then paste post_copy exactly as written, with all three hashtags, and post.
Paste the sources block as the first comment within 60 seconds of posting.

Reply to every comment in the first hour. If someone says a candidate supports or opposes data centers, point to that candidate's own words on slides 03 to 05 and to the KTUU link, because the deck claims only what the six told Alaska's News Source. If someone asks who voted no in the 6-1 vote, say the roll call wasn't found.
Fairness note. All six candidates get equal room in the deck, so reply evenly. Don't endorse, rank or criticize any candidate, and don't answer who to vote for.
After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts for the ledger.
editor_notes_for_email: Timing first. October 6th is election day in the Fairbanks North Star Borough, and the deck says 'Tuesday' on the cover, on slides 08 and 09 and in the document title. It only works posted Monday, October 5th, or early Tuesday before polls close at 8 p.m. After the vote, don't post it as is. On sourcing, the 6-1 vote and all six candidates' stances and quotes come from a single Alaska's News Source (KTUU) story dated September 29th; the borough's sample ballot confirms the six names and seats, and the Clerk's action memorandum records the adoption with no tally, so the deck credits the 6-1 to the station. The deck takes no side on any candidate. On the date, this run is filed as October 3rd although it ran on the evening of October 1st, Anchorage time, because runs/2026-10-01 and runs/2026-10-02 were already taken by earlier firings that day.
